title: Committee of Supply − Head Q (Ministry of Communications and Information)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply − Head Q (Ministry of Communications and Information)

sections.label: SME digital challenges and support
sections.summary: SMEs struggle to compete digitally amid economic slowdown, and the MP seeks an update on initiatives to help them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Many small and medium enterprises (SMEs) are trying to find their way in trying to win over customers and compete against competitors who have mastered the digital realm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: The impact of the current economic slowdown has not helped as most SMEs I have spoken to are more focused today on the issue of everyday survival to retain their current business and pay their employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: With the recent Committee on the Future Economy (CFE) report highlighting the shift to a digital economy, I would like to seek the Ministry's update on its initiative to help SMEs in particular which face more constraints and have less resources to help themselves.

sections.label: Industry transformation game-changing initiatives
sections.summary: The MP asks whether the Ministry has game-changing initiatives for industry transformation and what they are.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Specifically on industry transformation, I would like to find out if the Ministry has any game-changing initiatives and, if so, what would these be?

sections.label: ICT manpower initiatives update
sections.summary: The MP requests an update on ICT manpower initiatives announced at last year's Committee of Supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Besides SMEs, it is also important that we help Singaporeans maximise the opportunities presented by the digital wave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Also, I would like to request the Ministry to provide an update on the information and communications technology (ICT) manpower initiatives that it announced at the Committee of Supply (COS) last year.

sections.label: Civil servants digital capabilities training
sections.summary: The Government announced that 10,000 civil servants will be trained in digital capabilities to support innovation and entrepreneurial spirit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Chairman, the Government has announced that 10,000 civil servants will be trained up in digital capabilities to better support innovation and cultivate the entrepreneurial spirit.

sections.label: Chamber and IMDA SME digitalisation
sections.summary: The Chamber and IMDA have long worked together on IT adoption and iSPRINT, and hope to continue driving the SMEs Go Digital Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For many years now, the Chamber and IMDA have worked closely together to help SMEs adopt infocomm technology (IT) and promote the Increase SME Productivity with Infocomm Adoption and Transformation (iSPRINT) initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This has helped us to accumulate valuable experiences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This time, we hope to continue to work closely with IMDA to drive the "SMEs Go Digital Programme" in a big way.

sections.label: MCI and IMDA SME digital transformation
sections.summary: The MP asks how MCI and IMDA plan to help SMEs with digital transformation, citing Budget-supported sectors and the SME Technology Hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Budget has already announced certain sectors which will receive support first, including retail, food services, logistics and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Everyone must work together, relying on the capacity of the SME Technology Hub and leveraging the assistance of the "SMEs Go Digital Programme", so that they may discover the benefits of digitalisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How are the Ministry of Communication and Information (MCI) and IMDA planning to help SMEs with the digital transformation?

sections.label: TechSkills Accelerator and IT employability
sections.summary: MCI is asked how TeSA will improve IT staff employability beyond the announced Industry Transformation Maps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Last year, the TechSkills Accelerator (TeSA) was announced as an initiative to fill tech positions with Singaporean talents, through targeted training and job matching.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Can MCI elaborate on how TeSA will be used to improve employability of IT staff, on top of the Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs) that have been announced in the Budget?

sections.label: PDPA compliance and Smart Nation data
sections.summary: MCI is asked how it will help businesses, especially SMEs, comply with PDPA and how Singaporeans' personal data is protected in Smart Nation initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Can MCI share how it plans to further help businesses, especially SMEs, better comply with their data protection obligations under PDPA without any adverse effects?

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Second, what measures have been taken to ensure the protection of personal data of Singaporeans embarking on the Smart Nation initiatives?

sections.label: Parliamentary debate video streaming
sections.summary: The Government is asked whether it would consider live video streaming and a searchable video archive of Parliamentary debates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Specifically, I would like to ask the Government if it would consider live video streaming and a searchable video archive of Parliamentary debates.

sections.label: Citizen-state relations and speed cameras
sections.summary: The speaker says streaming would improve citizen-state relations and asks the Police to install more portable speed cameras in the constituency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I believe it will improve citizen-state relations in a significant way and improve public discussions about policy trade-offs and the understanding of Singaporeans about Parliamentary affairs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I asked the Police whether they could install more portable speed cameras within the constituency so that the need for constant patrolling by the Traffic Police can be reduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Despite the fact that cameras are so common nowadays, to date, the portable speed camera is not yet installed.

sections.label: Wireless CCTVs for illegal parking
sections.summary: The question asks whether the latest wireless technology can be used to install more CCTVs at lower cost to deter illegal parking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Can we use the latest wireless technology to install more such CCTVs at lower costs so as to deter illegal parking which obstructs other road users?

sections.label: Data technology, SingPass and seniors
sections.summary: The passage urges more investment in digital and data technology and describes difficulties seniors face using SingPass, 2FA and OneKey tokens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) can also analyse commuter data from the bus transport operators to determine where there is peak demand for buses on normal days, so that the bus companies can despatch buses to places where there is high commuter ridership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to consider investing more on digital and data technology so that it can continue to deliver essential services to the public and yet keep the costs of human capital low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One recent example is the difficulties that some seniors still face in trying to use SingPass and activating two-factor authentication (2FA).

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Seniors without mobile phones need to apply for the OneKey token.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In many cases, the only practical option for seniors who are unable to apply for the OneKey token online is to visit one of the two OneKey offices in Alexandra and Tanjong Pagar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is the case, notwithstanding the onsite assistance available at the 25 Citizen Connect Centres in Singapore who can help with applying for SingPass but not OneKey tokens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The process may prove cumbersome particularly for several groups of people, such as seniors who are not tech-savvy, those with low levels of education, those who are not conversant in English, those who do not own mobile phones and those who may have difficulties getting around.

sections.label: Leverage over overseas content producers
sections.summary: Singapore has limited leverage over overseas producers even when their content may harm religious or racial harmony.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Unlike local content producers, who have to comply with our laws, Singapore will often have limited leverage over overseas producers, even if they are creating content that might harm religious or racial harmony in Singapore.

sections.label: Germany Facebook fake news fines
sections.summary: Germany has floated fining Facebook €500,000 for each piece of fake news it fails to take down.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Germany has floated the idea of fining Facebook €500,000 for every single piece of "fake news" that it fails to take down.

sections.label: Working with content distributors
sections.summary: The question asks how the Ministry intends to work with content distributors to protect racial and religious harmony from fake news.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: How does the Ministry intend to approach working with content distributors to protect Singapore's racial and religious harmony from the scourge of fake news?

sections.label: Fake news racial religious risk
sections.summary: For Singapore, the risk of fake news exploiting racial and religious sentiment is real, and the speaker looks forward to hearing from the Ministry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: For a young country like Singapore, the risk of fake news exploiting racial and religious sentiment is real.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The situation is challenging but I look forward to hearing from the Ministry on this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This is a hot topic that governments around the world are starting to grapple with, and it is an exciting opportunity for Singapore to lead the world in creating a sound yet resilient regulatory regime.

sections.label: Restructured Statutory Boards and cybersecurity strategy
sections.summary: IDA and MDA were restructured into IMDA and GovTech, and Prime Minister Lee launched the Singapore Cybersecurity Strategy in October.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: First, we restructured our Statutory Boards, the Infocomm Development Authority (IDA) and the Media Development Authority (MDA), to form two new entities: IMDA and GovTech.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: We cannot be a Smart Nation if we remain open and vulnerable to cyberattacks.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Hence, in October, Prime Minister Lee launched the Singapore Cybersecurity Strategy to build a resilient and trusted cyber environment.

sections.label: IMDA TeSA ICT skills
sections.summary: Last year IMDA launched TeSA to help the workforce acquire new ICT skills such as cybersecurity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Last year, IMDA launched TeSA to help our workforce acquire new ICT skills, such as cybersecurity, so that they can secure better paying jobs and grow in their careers.

sections.label: Old Tea Hut sales system
sections.summary: 25% of Old Tea Hut's daily sales go through this system, raising overall sales 15% and speeding new outlet openings.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Due to the increased convenience that its customers experience, 25% of the company's daily sales are made via this system.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: This has allowed Old Tea Hut to increase its overall sales by 15% and more quickly open new outlets.

sections.label: Robinson's and SME savings
sections.summary: Robinson's saved 85% of manual supplier transaction time, and each SME redeployed two admin headcounts on average.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: By integrating on the same system, Robinson's saved 85% of the time used to manually process their numerous transactions with suppliers, while each SME, on average, was able to redeploy two admin headcounts to other tasks.

sections.label: Accredited companies programme results
sections.summary: By end February the programme accredited 17 companies, helping them generate Government project opportunities worth over $60 million.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: As of end February, the programme has accredited 17 companies in areas like video and data analytics, robotics and energy management, helping them generate Government project opportunities worth over $60 million.

sections.label: IMDA expanding accreditation programme
sections.summary: IMDA will expand the programme beyond the public sector to enterprise sectors and beyond startups to small high-growth SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Due to these accredited companies' success, IMDA will now be expanding the programme's focus beyond the public sector to the enterprise sectors, such as real estate and finance.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: It will also expand beyond accrediting startups to include small high-growth SMEs.

sections.label: TeSA upskilling professionals
sections.summary: As of mid-February 2017, TeSA enabled over 10,000 professionals to benefit from upskilling and reskilling opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: As of mid-February 2017, TeSA has enabled over 10,000 professionals to benefit from upskilling and reskilling opportunities.

sections.label: TeSA CLT partners and placement
sections.summary: TeSA's CLT programmes have high placement rates and over 15 partner companies, with SAS Institute and Deloitte and Touche Enterprise Risk Services newly added.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Having completed his on-the-job training, Alvin is now enjoying his work as a Security Consultant with Singapore Technologies (ST) Electronics.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: I am delighted to announce that TeSA's CLT programmes continue to have high placement rates and am pleased to add that our number of industry partners continues to grow.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: TeSA has partnered over 15 CLT companies, including Singtel, Accel, Quann and Optimum Solutions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Two new partners are SAS Institute and Deloitte and Touche Enterprise Risk Services, which will offer training in data analytics and cybersecurity respectively.

sections.label: Student enrolment since launch
sections.summary: About 800 students have enrolled since its launch last year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: About 800 students have enrolled since its launch last year.

sections.label: Cybersecurity growth sector projections
sections.summary: Cybersecurity was identified as an emerging growth sector projected to grow at 9.3% CAGR to about $900 million and potentially provide over 5,000 additional job openings by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Cybersecurity was identified as an emerging growth sector as it is projected to grow at 9.3% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) to about $900 million and could potentially provide over 5,000 additional job openings by 2020.

sections.label: Cybersecurity Professional Scheme
sections.summary: The Government will introduce a Cybersecurity Professional Scheme, centrally managed by CSA, to attract, develop and retain public sector cybersecurity practitioners deployed across agencies.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: To complement these manpower development efforts, the Government will introduce a Cybersecurity Professional Scheme to attract, develop and retain cybersecurity practitioners in the public sector.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Centrally managed by CSA, the scheme will develop a core of cybersecurity specialists to be deployed across agencies to support Singapore's cyber defences.

sections.label: Consultation and Broadcasting Act update
sections.summary: Consultation with some key stakeholders has started, wider public consultation will follow soon, and the Broadcasting Act will be updated this year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: We have started consulting some key stakeholders and will do a wider public consultation very soon.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: We will also update the Broadcasting Act (BA) this year.

sections.label: 2013 online news licensing scheme
sections.summary: One example is the 2013 online news licensing scheme for accountability and responsibility in news reporting.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: One example is the 2013 online news licensing scheme for accountability and responsibility in news reporting.

sections.label: Harmonising infocomm and media legislation
sections.summary: For the longer term, the Government remains committed to harmonising legislation for a converged infocomm and media environment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: For the longer term, we remain committed to harmonising our legislation for a converged infocomm and media environment.

sections.label: GovTech establishment and leadership
sections.summary: The establishment of GovTech last year is key to pushing these efforts, and GovTech will lead in several areas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The establishment of GovTech last year is key to giving these efforts a push, and GovTech will lead in several areas.

sections.label: GovTech API Exchange and Ask Jamie
sections.summary: GovTech is building an API Exchange to facilitate data sharing, and Ask Jamie is a Virtual Assistant live on 32 Government websites.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: As a result, GovTech is building an API Exchange (APEX) to facilitate such data sharing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Ms Sun asked also about what is being done to systematically integrate new applications to existing Government services. ''Ask Jamie'' is one example.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: It is a Virtual Assistant service that GovTech has developed in collaboration with various Government agencies, and is currently live on 32 Government websites, including the Ministry of Education (MOE), the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) and the Ministry of Health (MOH).

sections.label: GovTech ICT capability and talent programmes
sections.summary: GovTech will build ICT capability centres in data science, infrastructure, software and IoT, and put in place talent development programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: GovTech will build up ICT capability centres in a variety of areas, focusing on data science, Government ICT infrastructure, software development and the Internet of Things.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: GovTech will put in place a series of talent development programmes, such as the Smart Nation Fellowship Programme, and use its national projects to provide on-the-job training to its officers.

sections.label: IMDA Data Innovation Programme Office
sections.summary: IMDA will establish a Data Innovation Programme Office, which will introduce a Data Sandbox for companies to share data securely.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: IMDA will establish a Data Innovation Programme Office (DIPO) to lead this effort.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: One of the ways DIPO will do this is to introduce a Data Sandbox, which will provide a neutral and trusted platform for companies to share data securely without threatening their individual interests.

sections.label: PDPC reviewing Act and SME kits
sections.summary: PDPC will review the Act and develop Data Protection starter kits to help SMEs, engaging them through TACs and forums.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) will be actively reviewing the Act in light of the lessons learned over the past two years and the needs of the industry today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: PDPC will develop Data Protection starter kits to help SMEs kickstart their data protection practices within their companies, engage SMEs through the TACs and sector-specific forums, and provide more affirmative guidance to give certainty and clarity on what is permissible.

sections.label: Expanding Home Access Programme
sections.summary: IMDA is expanding the Home Access Programme to benefit a further 16,000 low-income households, in addition to the existing 8,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: IMDA already has a variety of programmes in place.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We are expanding the Home Access Programme, which provides low-income households with low-cost broadband connectivity at home and a tablet, to benefit a further 16,000 households, in addition to the existing 8,000 households on the current programme.

sections.label: AI replaces analysts, reskilling programme
sections.summary: DC Frontiers' AI took over its analysts' jobs, and the company reskills and redeploys those workers to keep them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The artificial intelligence (AI) programme that it has built has now taken over the jobs of their own analysts who were making the AI machine faster, sharper and better.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: DC Frontiers had seen this coming, embraced this change and now has a proactive, structured programme in place to reskill and redeploy its own workers and analysts and keep them within the company.

sections.label: Hearing-impaired app by De Bao
sections.summary: De Bao is hearing-impaired and designed an app that transcribes conversations in real-time for the hearing-impaired.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: De Bao is hearing-impaired and has designed an app for the hearing-impaired which transcribes conversations in real-time.

sections.label: De Bao's apps and IMDA
sections.summary: De Bao has over 15 applications and became a software developer; IMDA looks at promoting technology use among persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: From there, he has now a portfolio of over 15 different applications and went on to become a software developer.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: With De Bao's experience, IMDA is looking at ways to better promote the use of technology amongst persons with disabilities.

sections.label: Mediacorp PSB funding and online competition
sections.summary: The passage notes Mediacorp faces new competition from Netflix and Amazon and asks how the Ministry ensures increased funding delivers PSB outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
sentences.text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 5.20 pm until 5.40 pm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: It is important to note that our national broadcaster faces new challenges in competing for citizen attention, compared to new and emerging Internet content and service providers, such as Netflix and Amazon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: While Mediacorp has started going digital on Toggle, how does the Ministry ensure that the increased funding delivers intended PSB outcomes and that PSB programmes continue to stay relevant and viable, especially with the younger audiences moving online to consume overseas content?

sections.label: Vernacular language programme spending
sections.summary: The passage asks how spending differs among Mandarin, Malay and Tamil programmes to keep them relevant to younger Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: How different has the spending been among programmes from the vernacular languages − Mandarin, Malay and Tamil − especially to keep its relevance within the next generation of Singaporeans?

sections.label: IMDA film industry private funding
sections.summary: The passage asks what IMDA does to incentivise private film funding and whether it would consider a dollar-for-dollar co-investment scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: What measure is IMDA taking to incentivise and promote private sector funding for the film industry, including novel funding sources?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would IMDA consider a co-investment scheme whereby the state can match private investors dollar-for-dollar, so as to kickstart the growth of movie private funding?

sections.label: IDA MDA restructured into GovTech IMDA
sections.summary: IDA and MDA were restructured into GovTech and IMDA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: IDA and MDA were restructured into GovTech and IMDA.

sections.label: IMDA freelancer talent assistance schemes
sections.summary: IMDA has introduced talent assistance schemes for freelancers to deepen their expertise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: IMDA has introduced talent assistance schemes for freelancers to deepen their expertise.

sections.label: Government investment in Mediapolis
sections.summary: The Government has invested millions into Mediapolis, Singapore's media hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government has invested millions into Mediapolis, which is Singapore's media hub.

sections.label: Mediacorp outsourcing and PSB transparency
sections.summary: Mediacorp outsources 40% of public service-funded projects to independent production companies, with industry calls for more transparency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mediacorp outsources 40% of public service-funded projects to independent production companies in the private sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There have been calls from the industry for more transparency with regard to the quantum and projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There is much expectation that with the establishment of IMDA, the agency can now make public the projects that are commissioned under the PSB Framework, as well as the contestable fund initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is a move in the right direction and will create more transparency and trust between broadcasters and production entities and build a more balanced and robust competitive environment that can only be good for the marketplace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This will also allow commissioners to be able to differentiate the strengths of the various production entities and deal with the best-in-class across different genres.

sections.label: Starhub pay-TV subscriber losses
sections.summary: Starhub's pay-TV business continues to lose subscribers, with 38,000 cutting the cord over 15 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Starhub's pay-TV business continues to lose subscribers as 7% of its subscribers, or 38,000 subscribers, have cut the cord over the last 15 months.

sections.label: Pay platform licensed football content
sections.summary: Last year, one pay platform decided to license the English Premier League and other football content to a new channel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Last year, one of our pay platforms decided to license the English Premier League and other football content to a new channel.

sections.label: Pay-TV rental rate increases
sections.summary: Subscribers are often told of increases to set-top box rental rates and channel packages, and Pay-TV platforms must accept their monopolistic dominance is gone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Despite these issues, ever so often, subscribers are told of increases to rental rates of set-top boxes and channel packages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Pay-TV platforms in Singapore need to accept that their days of monopolistic dominance are gone.

sections.label: Mediacorp operations review outcomes
sections.summary: The speaker asks what the outcomes of the Mediacorp operations review are and what changes Singaporeans can expect, noting Mediacorp's financial challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In principle, I would like Mediacorp to be financially independent, but Mediacorp faces serious challenges in delivering good quality content in a financially self-sustainable way.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It was announced at COS 2016 that there would be a review of the operations of Mediacorp to see how it can better position itself for the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: What are the outcomes of this review conducted by Mediacorp of its operations?

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: What changes can Singaporeans expect to see from this review?

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In last year's COS debates, Minister of State Chee Hong Tat announced that the Government would be enhancing its communications to the public across three dimensions, namely, Content, Platforms and Language.

sections.label: MCI public communications initiatives
sections.summary: MCI leads and coordinates this effort, and the speaker asks what other initiatives it has to improve whole-of-Government public communications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: MCI is responsible for leading and coordinating this effort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I am interested to know what other initiatives it has in mind to improve its public communications for the whole of Government.

sections.label: Outdoor adventure education consultation
sections.summary: The private outdoor adventure education industry was consulted so late that it could do little to counter-propose a decision affecting its businesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One example of a missed opportunity was with the private outdoor adventure education industry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Many were surprised by the announcement last year that the Government was going to provide outdoor adventure education to students.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They were consulted but so late in the process that there was very little they could do to counter-propose a decision presented to them that would impact their businesses quite significantly.

sections.label: Earlier consultations before policies set
sections.summary: The first suggestion is to conduct consultations earlier, before policies are set in stone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, conduct consultations earlier before policies are set in stone.

sections.label: More diverse dialogue viewpoints
sections.summary: The second suggestion is to compose dialogues and focus groups with more obvious diversity in viewpoints.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, compose the dialogues and focus groups with more obvious diversity in viewpoints.

sections.label: Feedback on infotainment series
sections.summary: MCI and elderly residents' feedback showed both series were well received and raised awareness of Government policies with some message retention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: Based on feedback shared by MCI and also the elderly residents that I spoke to, both series were not only well received as a form of infotainment, but there was definitely increased awareness of Government policies and there was also some retention of key messages as well.

sections.label: Reading habits and book access
sections.summary: Only 25 persons or 9% read a book over 100 pages, prompting suggestions to make eBooks free and broadcast book extracts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
sentences.text: Only 25 persons or 9% of them have read at least one book of more than 100 pages.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
sentences.text: This finding is, indeed, not surprising as many Singaporeans, especially adult Singaporeans, are losing interest or face increasing difficulty in finding time to read books.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
sentences.text: First, make eBooks easily available to Singaporeans and free of charge, if possible.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
sentences.text: Second, broadcast book extracts and reviews through smart phone applications and provide book delivery services or book pick-up services at Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) stations or supermarkets.

sections.label: Singaporeans in media productions
sections.summary: Singaporeans from ILM created effects for Star Wars, and Very Tay worked with HBO Asia on the series Sent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: For example, a team of Singaporeans from Industry Light and Magic (ILM) − this is the visual effects studio arm of Lucasfilm − created ground-breaking animation and visual effects for the blockbuster film "Star Wars: The Force Awakens".

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: HBO Asia's latest original comedy series called "Sent" is the first series where a local media company, Very Tay, has worked hand in hand with HBO Asia through the entire process from development, writing to production.

sections.label: IMDA Production Assistance Grant
sections.summary: The IMDA Production Assistance Grant co-funds up to 40% of a project's qualifying expenses to help media companies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: IMDA's Production Assistance Grant is one such scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: It is a co-funding scheme which supports up to 40% of a project's qualifying expenses and this helps our media companies.

sections.label: Media Manpower Plan announcement
sections.summary: Minister Yaacob had earlier announced a Media Manpower Plan with four key thrusts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Minister Yaacob had earlier announced a Media Manpower Plan with four key thrusts.

sections.label: Skills framework for media professionals
sections.summary: A skills framework for media professionals will be developed to enhance the media industry's attractiveness.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Second, we will enhance the media industry's attractiveness by developing a skills framework for media professionals.

sections.label: Media freelancer payment standards
sections.summary: IMDA and NTUC are developing a tripartite standard for procuring media freelancer services, with subsidised mediation for contractual disputes like late or non-payment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: First, IMDA and NTUC are developing a tripartite standard by this year for the procurement of services from media freelancers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In partnership with the Singapore Mediation Centre, IMDA will also provide subsidised mediation services to help resolve disputes between media companies and freelancers on contractual matters, including late payment and, sometimes, non-payment.

sections.label: Funding tied to payment practices
sections.summary: Media companies and Mediacorp PSB production houses must adopt good industry practices to qualify for Government grants and PSB funding, with IMDA acting against wrongful payment delays.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This includes media companies which receive Government funding, as well as production houses which work with Mediacorp on PSB programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We will start by requiring media companies to adopt the above-mentioned good industry practices if they want to qualify for Government grants and PSB funding.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: IMDA will take action against companies that wrongfully delay or withhold payment to their staff and freelancers.

sections.label: Content Development Fund for PSB
sections.summary: IMDA and Mediacorp will establish a Content Development Fund to encourage experimentation with new content formats, including AR and VR technologies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: To keep PSB content offerings relevant and fresh, IMDA and Mediacorp will establish a Content Development Fund to encourage more experimentation with new content formats, including the use of new technologies like augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR).

sections.label: Toggle content and Okto repositioning
sections.summary: Good Toggle content can be re-telecast on FTA TV, and Mediacorp will reposition Okto as a children and sports channel.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Good content developed for Toggle can then be re-telecast on FTA TV, so that TV audiences can also enjoy them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: I am pleased to inform Mr Zaqy Mohamad that Mediacorp will reposition Okto as a children and sports channel.

sections.label: Young creative talent pipeline
sections.summary: IMDA will partner Mediacorp to build a pipeline of young creative talent for the media industry.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: To invest for the future, IMDA will partner Mediacorp to build a pipeline of young creative talent for the media industry.

sections.label: Mediacorp increases outsourcing collaboration
sections.summary: Starting this year, Mediacorp will enhance collaboration with industry players by increasing the amount of outsourcing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Starting from this year, Mediacorp will enhance its collaboration with industry players by increasing the amount of outsourcing.

sections.label: Quality local content and PSB funds
sections.summary: The speaker wants a win-win arrangement for quality local content and encourages industry players to tap the PSB Contestable Funds Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Ultimately, what we want is to have a win-win arrangement to bring quality local content to our viewers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: I also encourage all industry players to tap on the PSB Contestable Funds Scheme to create quality PSB content.

sections.label: SPH circulation increase 2015-2016
sections.summary: From 2015 to 2016, SPH achieved a 2.8% increase in average daily circulation for print and digital editions combined.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: From 2015 to 2016, SPH achieved a 2.8% increase in its average daily circulation for both print and digital editions combined.

sections.label: Project Lapis Sagu film contest
sections.summary: MCI's crowdsourcing film contest Project Lapis Sagu, supported by four local directors, received more than 1,200 entries on social integration story ideas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: For example, MCI has started a crowdsourcing initiative called Project Lapis Sagu, a film contest that invited the public to submit story ideas on fostering awareness and understanding on social integration.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: With support from four well-known local film directors − Eric Khoo, Kelvin Tong, K Rajagopal and Sanif Olek − we received more than 1,200 entries.

sections.label: Seniors enjoy Government communications programmes
sections.summary: Seniors found the shows informative and entertaining, and similar content in Malay and Tamil is being developed to enhance Government communications.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Many seniors, including my residents, have told me that they enjoyed these shows and found them informative and entertaining.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: I am pleased to inform Mr Darryl David that we will continue with these programmes to enhance Government communications, and we are also developing similar content in Malay and Tamil.

sections.label: Online archival period lengthened since 2013
sections.summary: The online archival period for these videos was lengthened from one month to six months since 2013.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The online archival period for these videos has also been lengthened since 2013.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: It used to be one month; now it is six months.

sections.label: Budget Statement live viewership figures
sections.summary: Fewer than 10% of Parliamentary highlights viewers watched the Budget Statement live, and under 1% watched it live via web-streaming.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Even for a major speech like the Budget Statement, the number of people who watched it "live" is less than 10% of those who watched the Parliamentary highlights on the news that evening.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: And less than 1% of all viewers watched the Budget Statement "live" using web-streaming, and this is the Budget Statement − it is a major speech.

sections.label: NLB reading workshops and talks
sections.summary: NLB will launch Raise a Reader workshops for parents, and with Lianhe Zaobao will launch monthly talks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: NLB will launch "Raise a Reader" workshops this year for parents to learn more about the resources available at our libraries and how to choose appropriate books for their children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Weekly news reading interest group attracted a good following since its launch in March 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This year, NLB and Lianhe Zaobao will launch a series of monthly talks.

sections.label: Tampines Regional Library reopening
sections.summary: Tampines Regional Library will reopen in August, with Chou Sing Chu Foundation sponsoring most Chinese Children's Collection books.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Tampines Regional Library will reopen in August this year and Chou Sing Chu Foundation will be sponsoring the majority of the books in the Chinese Children's Collection.

sections.label: National Reading Movement mother tongues
sections.summary: Through the National Reading Movement, Singaporeans will be encouraged to read in mother tongue languages to strengthen bilingualism.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Through the National Reading Movement, we will continue to encourage Singaporeans to read in mother tongue languages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This is a worthwhile effort to strengthen bilingualism and develop Singapore's competitive edge.

sections.label: Digital book borrowing increase
sections.summary: Over 100,000 digital books are borrowed monthly from NLB's online collections, a 38% increase from last year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Every month, on average, over 100,000 digital books are borrowed from NLB's online collections.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Compared to last year, we have seen an increase of 38%.

sections.label: National Reading Movement campaign support
sections.summary: The five-year National Reading Movement has over 430,000 pledges and support from more than 380 organisations encouraging staff to Read@Work.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Last year, we embarked on the National Reading Movement, a five-year campaign to encourage adults and seniors to read and for citizens to read in their mother tongues.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Over 430,000 people so far have made this pledge.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: More than 380 organisations have also supported the reading campaign in various ways by encouraging their staff to Read@Work.

sections.label: Resident reading survey results
sections.summary: Sixty-nine percent of residents read at least one book last year, and 56% of book readers borrow from libraries.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Sixty-nine percent of residents surveyed said they read at least one book in the past year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Eighty percent said they read more than once a week, be it books, magazines, news online or social media.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Only 19% read books more than once a week and most did not find reading as stimulating as audio-visual content.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Fifty-six percent of those who read books borrow them from our libraries.

sections.label: NLB and Bosses Network
sections.summary: NLB will work with an informal group of SME owners, the Bosses Network, to run a business acumen series in Chinese.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: For example, NLB will work with an informal group of SME owners, called the Bosses Network, to run a business acumen series conducted in Chinese.

sections.label: GovTech digital services for citizens
sections.summary: GovTech will lead by creating more Government digital services that make life easier for citizens and keep the citizen at the centre of user experience.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: GovTech will lead the way by creating more Government digital services that help make life easier for citizens on the go and that keep the citizen − the young, the old, the technology-savvy or not − at the centre of user experience.

sections.label: Government digital transformation and heartware
sections.summary: Government will emphasise integrated digital transformation with GovTech at the centre, working with 10,000 digital-ready officers, and will complement hardware and software with heartware.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Within the Government, we will also be placing more emphasis on driving Government digital transformation and technology adoption in a more integrated manner, with GovTech at the centre of these efforts, and working in concert with 10,000 digital-ready officers across the public sector.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: In all our efforts, the Government will always be guided by the need to ensure that we help workers, businesses and citizens transition smoothly and benefit from technology.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: We will always be aware of the need to complement the hardware and software with heartware so that technology helps bring us together rather than drive us apart and so that technology serves us and not enslaves us.

sections.label: Coming together for Smart Nation
sections.summary: Only by coming together will Singapore realise its Smart Nation vision and harness technology to improve as many lives as possible.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: Only when we come together will we realise our Smart Nation vision and ensure that we harness technology to improve as many lives as possible.

sections.label: TeSA and mid-career professionals
sections.summary: TeSA offers opportunities through the Professional Conversion Programme for mid-career professionals, and IMDA with TeSA will consider all professionals who want to transition.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: First, on the transformation for our senior career professionals, as per the example of Mr Alvin Koh whom I mentioned in my speech, there are a lot of opportunities through TeSA, for example, under the Professional Conversion Programme (PCP).

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: We can help people who are mid-career, who may have lost their jobs or want to have a change, preferably if they come from a sector which is related with the Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) sector, it would be much easier.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: But IMDA is prepared, as I said earlier, working with TeSA to consider all professionals who may want to make that transition.

sections.label: Non-profit organisations IMDA support study
sections.summary: IMDA is asked to study whether other non-profit organisations can benefit from some of its support.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: On the second question as to whether or not other organisations which are non-profit can benefit from some of the support by IMDA, let me ask IMDA to study this.

sections.label: Translation in multilingual society
sections.summary: Translation matters in a multilingual society with four official languages, and the National Translation Committee works with schools, education institutions and media partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Translation is a very important area because we live in a multilingual society and we have got four official languages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: One of the things that the National Translation Committee, which I chair, does is to work closely with our partners, in particular, the schools and the education institutions as well as our media partners because these are areas where you have got resources and also to reach out to our young people.

sections.label: Tamil translation review
sections.summary: The speaker says they are working closely with other communities and recently announced a review of the Tamil translation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We are also working closely with other communities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I recently announced the review of the Tamil translation.

sections.label: No edits to speech videos
sections.summary: There is no edit done to video clips of speeches, except where there are pauses or very local issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: To the Member's first question, the answer is yes, there is no edit done to the video clips of speeches, except for those places where there are some pauses or when certain issues are very local issues.

sections.label: Newspaper satisfaction survey numbers
sections.summary: In the same study, newspaper ranking improved from sixth in 2014 to first in 2015, with satisfaction rising from 74.8% to 78.9%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The numbers that I cited in my speech where I said the newspapers' ranking improved from sixth in 2014 to first in 2015, it is in the same study.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Of the respondents in 2014, 74.8% said they were satisfied with newspapers' content and, in 2015, this number went up to 78.9%.

sections.label: Use of multiple languages
sections.summary: Mr Kok asked about the use of multiple languages, an idea the speaker says they will certainly discuss.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Mr Kok also asked about the use of multiple languages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: That is a very interesting idea which we will certainly discuss.

sections.label: No dominant library genre
sections.summary: No one genre is dominant based on the observed pattern, primarily because library users come from a wide cross section of the community.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: To answer the Member's question, there is no one genre which is dominant, based on the pattern that we observed, and primarily because the library users are basically from a wide cross section or our community.

sections.label: Public access to Budget information
sections.summary: The current arrangement provides timely public access to Budget videos and information, and most people prefer TV news highlights over live viewing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Our assessment is that the current arrangement has sufficient avenues for the public to have access to the information, to the video clips, and these are put in a timely manner, that very night itself, the news highlights are up in three hours, all the videos are up by 8.00 am the next morning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Our sense is that, in terms of information availability and also convenience of viewing for the public, going in to look for what they are interested in, what they want to watch, the site is well-organised and well-sorted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The current data that we have collected, as I shared in my speech about the Budget Statement, showed that most people still prefer to view it through the TV during the news highlights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Not many want to view the Budget Statement "live" and even fewer view it "live" streaming.
